resources.string: Every layout that you turn on is its own input mode. Use the 🌐 key or a spacebar swipe to change between them.
Get emoji keywords and prediction data for the languages that you use

With this on, the keyboard downloads the small files a language needs, when you add it and when a new one is published: emoji keywords, so emoji search answers in your language, and word-pair data, which makes predictions better. Word lists for your languages download too, but only on Wi-Fi or another unmetered connection, and one you deleted stays deleted. With this off, nothing is downloaded until you ask for it on a language screen.
Make your own key grid, or start from a built-in one
Switch to a phonetic layout mid-word and the letters that you typed convert too
After your languages, holding or swiping the spacebar can reach the language settings or your other keyboards

Hold the spacebar and the preview above it lists your languages. With this set, one more stop follows the last of them: a gear that opens this screen, or a keyboard that opens Android\'s list of keyboards. Drag onto it and lift to go there. A swipe along the spacebar reaches it too. A quick flick still moves one language at a time, so only a swipe that keeps going past your last language lands on it. With two languages, the swipe then walks three stops in a line instead of toggling. The list and carousel pickers show the gear as a row of their own, next to Other keyboards.

Phonetic layouts such as Avro, Hindi phonetic and Khipro spell their script with roman letters. When you notice halfway through a word that you are still on your Latin keyboard, switching language now converts the letters that you already typed instead of leaving them as they are: type "tu", switch to Avro, and the word reads তু, so "mi" after it finishes তুমি. Turn this off if you often switch language right after an English word and before typing a space, because that word is carried over as well.
Set the language for an app

Pick an app and the language it should open on, or Remember last. A rule wins over Remember language per app for that app. You can still change language while you type there, and the rule applies again the next time you come back from another app.
Open each app with the layout that you used there last

When you change language while you type in an app, the keyboard remembers your choice for that app. The keyboard uses that language again the next time that you type there. You can change language with the 🌐 key, a spacebar swipe or the picker. Apps where you selected no language use your last language. A field that requires Latin letters, such as a password box, still overrides this. A field that gives its own language also overrides this.
List languages in the Android switcher
Add each language to the input method switcher of the system

The keyboard registers every layout that you turn on as an Android input method subtype. The \"Choose input method\" sheet of the system then lists them, and you can change between them there. Turn this off to keep language switching inside the keyboard only, with the 🌐 key, a spacebar swipe or the picker. The keyboard then tells the system only the language that you type in, and the sheet lists it as \"WM Keyboard\" instead of as one language name. A system spell checker that uses the system language then checks the language that you type in.\n\nTo register a language and to make it switchable are two different things. Android lists only the languages that something turns on. Until then, Android selects them itself from the languages of your device, and it usually selects one. On Android 14 and newer, the keyboard turns them all on for you. On older versions, select them by hand in the system settings with the row below.

This puts the app name in front of the language in the label of the switcher. Android decides how it styles the label and the app name, such as which one is bold or grey. This setting changes only the label text, not that styling.
Select languages in the system settings
The list of Android. Use it only if the switcher looks wrong
Android 13 and older: select each language here, or the switcher shows only one
Open emoji with one press from the top bar
Tools that stay in the top bar while the suggestions show. Drag to change their order
Put the toolbox first among these buttons, so it is one tap away while the suggestions show
Put these buttons after the suggestions, at the far end of the strip
Size the buttons beside the suggestions apart from the toolbar\'s tools
How wide each button beside the suggestions is
How big the icon in each button beside the suggestions is

The emoji button stays visible in the top bar, also while the suggestions show. The emoji panel has a tab for each category. You can search in English and Bengali, and in any language that you add a keyword pack for. Press and hold an emoji for the skin tone variants.
Hide the toolbar and move the category tabs up, next to a back button

The emoji panel fills the whole keyboard. The toolbar, the emoji row and the symbol row go away. The category tabs move into the row that they leave, next to a back button. Turn this off to keep the toolbar in reach while you select emoji.
Show emoji while you type. The word birthday suggests 🎂 🎉 🥳
Emoji that match appear at the end of the suggestion strip while you type. This works in English and in any language whose keywords you have. %1$s also suggests 🎂.
What happens to the word that you typed. Hold the suggestion for the other one

\"Replace word\" changes the word that you typed to the emoji. If you type birthday and press 🎂, only 🎂 stays, as in Gboard. \"Keep word\" adds the emoji after the word: birthday 🎂.\n\nHold an emoji suggestion to do the other one this time. With \"Replace word\" selected, a hold keeps the word. With \"Keep word\" selected, a hold replaces it.
Type birthday, press 🎂, and only 🎂 stays
Type birthday, press 🎂, and you get birthday 🎂
For toned emoji in the panel, the suggestions and the search

The keyboard shows toned emoji (👍, 🙏, 🧑…) with this Fitzpatrick tone in the grid of the emoji panel, the suggestion strip and the emoji search results. It also inserts them with that tone. An emoji that you selected a tone for keeps your tone while \"Override with last used\" is on. The first option (✋) keeps the neutral yellow base.
Use the tone that you selected last for an emoji, not the default

When this is on, and it is on by default, an emoji that you already selected a tone for keeps that tone everywhere: in the panel, the suggestions and the search. You select that tone from the press and hold popup of the emoji in the panel. The emoji does not use the default above. When this is off, the default skin tone always wins.
How the emoji picker is laid out
How wide each cell of the emoji grid is, at least. A smaller size fits more columns

The emoji panel fits as many columns as its width allows, and each cell is at least this wide. A smaller size packs more emoji on one screen. A larger size spreads them out, and each one is easier to hit. When the emoji size below needs more room than this, the cells grow to fit it.
How large the emoji panel draws each emoji

The size of the emoji in the grid of the emoji panel, on every tab and in the search results. The cells always keep enough room around each emoji, so a very large size can also mean fewer columns. The press and hold popup keeps its own size.
How many emoji go across one row

Auto fits as many columns as the grid size allows, so a wider screen shows more. A fixed number keeps each emoji in the same column on every screen. Arrange like sets this to match the keyboard you pick.
How tall each row of emoji is
Auto makes each row as tall as the emoji size needs. A fixed height, with fixed columns, makes the same swipe scroll to the same emoji as on the keyboard that Arrange like copied.
Return to the keyboard after you insert
Close the panel when you insert one emoji or paste one clip
By default, the emoji panel and the clipboard panel stay open, so that you can select several items. Turn this on to go back to the keys directly after one emoji or one clipboard paste.
Where the emoji, GIF and sticker panels show the buttons that go between them

The switch has one button for each of the emoji panel, the GIF panel and the sticker panel, so that you can go from one to the next directly. It is at the same place in all three panels. \"Bottom\" puts it in the bottom row, between ABC and the space bar. \"Top\" puts it at the end of the search row. The GIF button and the sticker button show only while those tools are on. If you changed the layout of the emoji panel, the switch is where your layout puts it. To add it, use the \"Emoji, GIF and sticker switch\" part in the panel layout editor.
Scroll through all the emoji, with a heading over each category

When this is on, the emoji panel is one list that you scroll from top to bottom. Each category starts with its name, and you go from one category to the next without a stop. The category tabs jump to a category and show the category that you are in. When this is off, each category is a page, and you swipe left or right to go to the next one.
How much taller than the keyboard the emoji, GIF and sticker panels open

A taller panel shows more emoji, GIFs and stickers at one time. The letters keep their own height, and the three panels have the same height, so the keyboard does not move when you go from one to the next. The panel never covers more than most of the screen, so on a short screen, or with the phone sideways, it can stay shorter than this.
The emoji key opens emoji, GIFs or stickers, the same as you left them

When this is on, the emoji key and the emoji tool open the panel of the three that you used last. If one of the three panels is open, they close it. When this is off, the emoji key always opens the emoji panel. The keyboard forgets the last panel when it restarts.
What the first tab of the emoji panel shows

\"Recent\" lists emoji in the order that you used them last. \"Most used\" puts the emoji that you use most often first. The keyboard always keeps your favourite emoji at the start of both lists. \"Off\" removes the tab, so the panel opens on the first emoji category.
In the order that you used them last
The emoji that you use most often come first
How narrow a category tab may get before the tabs scroll sideways. Less fits every tab on the screen
Your most used emoji at the top, then your recent ones, each under its own heading
No history tab. The panel opens on the first category
A button on the Recent tab that deletes the recents list
This adds a \"Clear recents\" button to the Recent tab of the emoji panel. It is off by default, to keep the tab clean.
A tab of text faces: ¯\\_(ツ)_/¯ and :-)

This adds a Kaomoji tab at the end of the tabs of the emoji panel. Kaomoji are Japanese style faces, such as (╯°□°）╯︵ ┻━┻. Emoticons are the Western ASCII ones, such as :-D and <3. Both are in one library that you can change: add your own faces, put them under tags, and sort them. If you press a face, the keyboard types it as plain text. It does not go into your emoji history.
Show the name of the emoji at the top of its press and hold popup

Press and hold an emoji to show its Unicode name, such as \"skull and crossbones\". The name appears above the favourite control and the variant controls. This helps you to see the difference between emoji that look almost the same.
Send a moving version of an emoji from its press and hold popup

Press and hold an emoji in the emoji panel to see the moving version, and a control that sends it as an image. The images are Noto Animated Emoji by Google, under the CC BY 4.0 licence. The keyboard downloads each one from Google when you ask for it, at about 800 KB. About 880 emoji have one, and the control does not appear for the others, or in an app that accepts no images.
Add a control that sends the emoji itself as a picture

Press and hold an emoji in the emoji panel to get a control that sends it as a picture, in the emoji font that you selected. This is useful when the other person has a device that draws the emoji differently, or cannot draw it at all. The keyboard draws the picture on your device and downloads nothing, except one time for the Google emoji font. The picture goes out in the same way as the stickers of the sticker tool. To change that, open Tools, then Stickers, then \"Send stickers as\". The control does not appear in an app that accepts no images.
Download or import keywords to search emoji in another language
A row of your own emoji, like Gboard

\"Own row\" keeps an emoji row between the toolbar and the keys at all times. \"Button\" adds a button at the right end of the toolbar. The button changes the suggestion strip to the emoji row. \"Off\" hides both.
No emoji row and no button for it
A button at the right end of the toolbar opens the row
The row stays between the toolbar and the keys
The emoji that you use most often
The emoji that you used last
Only the emoji that you marked as a favourite
How many fit across. A higher number packs them tighter

The row divides its width into this many slots and makes the emoji small enough to fit them. A higher number gives smaller emoji that are closer together. When scrolling is off, the row hides the emoji after the last slot. When scrolling is on, a swipe shows them.
Swipe sideways for the emoji after the visible ones

When this is on, and it is on by default, you can swipe the row sideways to reach the emoji after the visible ones. When this is off, the row does not move. It shows only the emoji that fit, so a sideways swipe cannot move it under your finger.
How emoji look on the keyboard itself

\"System\" uses the emoji pack of your device. On Samsung devices that is the Samsung set. \"Google\" downloads Noto Color Emoji, the standard Android look, one time through the system font provider, and keeps it on your device. \"Installed\" uses an emoji font from Addons, such as Twemoji or OpenMoji. \"Custom\" uses one emoji font file that you import below. The text that you send is always plain Unicode. Other apps and other devices draw it with their own emoji font.
The emoji pack of your device
Noto Color Emoji, the standard Android look
Emoji fonts from Addons or from your files, kept so that you can change between them
One emoji font file that you import below
Downloads the current Noto Color Emoji, with the newest emoji in it. About %1$s. The \"Google\" option above can only use the version that your device already has.
Version %1$s of Noto Color Emoji is out, with emoji that your copy does not have. About %2$s.
You did not import an emoji font. The keyboard uses the system font until you import one.
Hide emoji that your device cannot show
Skip emoji that show as a blank box in the panel, the search and the suggestions

Older devices, and some brands, have an emoji font that is older than the newest emoji. Those emoji then show as an empty \"tofu\" box. This setting hides every emoji that the emoji font of your device cannot draw. To see them all, set the emoji font above to \"Google\" (Noto Color Emoji). You can also install a complete emoji font from Addons, such as Twemoji or OpenMoji. WM Keyboard has no emoji font of its own. It uses the font that you select here.

The font that you selected above covers only the emoji that it was built with. Usually only the newest release has the newest emoji. The keyboard does not hide those emoji. It draws each one in the emoji font of your device, so you still see it, but in another style.
Find any character by its Unicode name
The emoji search also finds symbols, letters and marks by the words of their name

Type the words of a character\'s Unicode name in the emoji search and it appears after the emoji: em dash, copyright sign, greek small letter lambda, latin small letter a with ogonek. Every character of the Basic Multilingual Plane is covered, which is tens of thousands of letters, marks and symbols. Tapping one inserts it. This setting is off by default.
Tip: press and hold any emoji in the panel to make it a favourite or to select skin tones. For an emoji with two persons, such as 🤝, you can set the tone of each person.
No emoji fonts are installed. Install one from Addons, such as Twemoji or OpenMoji, or add a font file from your device.
How many emoji the history tab remembers

The history tab lists your favourites first and then the emoji you used most recently. Thirty two is about one row on a small phone and four on a tablet, so raise it if history feels too short. Lowering it trims the list straight away. This setting is 32 by default.
Forget recents, usage counts, favourites and skin tone picks
The history tab empties, your favourites are unpinned, and the skin tone picked for each emoji goes back to the default. Emoji themselves are not affected. This cannot be undone.
Set in Data saver, along with the other downloads
Pair a romanized language with the languages it is typed alongside

Adding a romanized language such as Banglish links it with the other languages that share its script, so suggestions come from both. The linking runs every time you add a language, which means a link you removed by hand would come back. Turn this off to keep your own choices. This setting is on by default.

%1$d apps have a language pinned to them

resources.string: Every app goes back to following your last used language. The setting that remembers them stays on, so apps will start being remembered again as you switch language inside them.
Reorder the tabs, hide the ones you never open, and arrange the emoji inside each

The emoji panel ships its categories in Unicode\'s own order, which is rarely the order you reach for them in. Drag a category to move its tab, and press the eye to hide a tab you never open. Press a category to arrange the emoji inside it: press and hold one, then drag it where you want it. The Recent tab and the Kaomoji tab are not listed here. Recent orders itself by use, and the Kaomoji tab has a page of its own, Kaomoji, on the Emoji panel page.
Put the tabs, the hidden ones and the emoji in every category back the way they shipped
Every category goes back to Unicode order, every hidden tab comes back, and the emoji inside every category go back to their catalogue order. Your recents, favourites and skin tones are not touched.
Press and hold an emoji, then drag it where you want it.
Put this category back in catalogue order
Put the tabs and the emoji in the order of Gboard, SwiftKey or HeliBoard

Pick the keyboard you used before, and the emoji panel gets its tabs, in its order, with each emoji where that keyboard puts it. The grid also changes to that keyboard\'s columns, row height and emoji size, so the same swipe scrolls to the same emoji. Some keyboards keep plants with the animals and the weather with travel and places. Those emoji then move to that tab, and a tab with nothing left in it is hidden. An emoji that keyboard does not have yet goes next to the emoji it follows. After you pick one, you can still drag tabs and emoji. Unicode puts everything back the way it shipped.
%1$s replaces the tab order, the hidden tabs, the emoji order and the grid size that you set. Your recents, favourites and skin tones do not change.
Add emoji that are newer than the keyboard, one at a time or from Unicode\'s emoji-test.txt

Each Unicode release adds new emoji. Until an update of WM Keyboard includes them, you can add them here. An added emoji shows at the end of its tab in the emoji panel. You can search for it by its name and keywords, make it a favourite, and it shows in Recent. When an update includes the emoji, its row here says so and you can delete it. Added emoji go into your backups and sync with your settings.
Paste the emoji, give it a name and keywords, and choose its tab
Add every emoji the keyboard does not have yet, from the list at unicode.org/Public/emoji/latest/emoji-test.txt
This file is not an emoji-test.txt from Unicode, or it could not be read.
There is nothing to add. The keyboard already has every emoji in this file.

Every emoji you added goes out of the emoji panel and out of search. Emoji the keyboard includes are not touched.
The keyboard already has this emoji, in %1$s.
Enter one emoji, with no spaces.
This is too long for one emoji.
Paste the emoji, or type it
Separate them with commas. Search finds the emoji by its name and by these words.
Tags, the edit buttons, your own faces and imports from Emotic
Show :-) and the other ASCII faces in a tab of their own
A row of tags at the top of the tab. Off shows one long list with a heading for each tag.
The tag the tab shows when you open the emoji panel
A column of buttons beside the faces: search, add, edit and tags
With the column off, the add, edit and tags buttons move to the end of the tag row, so you can still change your faces from the keyboard.
Type a tag, such as shrug or tableflip, to see its faces in the suggestions

The keyboard shows the faces of a tag when the word you type is the name of that tag. Your favourites and the faces you use most come first. If you press one, it goes in after your word, or in place of it, the same as an emoji suggestion.
Show the faces that match after the emoji in the search of the emoji panel
Add, change, sort and delete the faces in your library
Sort, hide, rename and delete the tags of the tag row
An Emotic export, a file from this keyboard, or a list with one face on each line
